tools.description: Create a folder on this computer for tracking legislation. You own it — it holds the data cloned so far and a plain-text file describing the topics you care about, and it can be published to GitHub or deleted at any time.
tools.name: setup_workspace
tools.title: Create your legislation workspace

tools.description: Report which jurisdictions have been cloned, how many bills and recorded votes each has, and what questions that data can and cannot answer.

jurisdictions.description: Jurisdictions to report on, as locale codes (`il`, `usa`) or Open Civic Data ids. Omit for everything already cloned.

tools.name: check_local_data
tools.title: See what data is on this computer

tools.description: Download legislation for one or more jurisdictions from public git repositories to this computer. No account, no API key, and no record of what you look up — every later question is answered from the local copy.

jurisdictions.description: Jurisdictions to clone, as locale codes: two-letter state codes (`il`, `wy`), `usa` for Congress, or `dc`, `pr`, `gu`, `vi`, `mp`.

tools.name: clone_government_data
tools.title: Privately clone government data

tools.description: Write the topics you care about into your workspace as reusable definitions. They are saved as plain YAML you can read, edit, and re-run yourself.

description.description: What this topic covers. Embedded and compared against every bill.

examples.description: Two or three sentences describing bills that should match.

exclude_keywords.description: Terms that disqualify a bill from this topic.

include_keywords.description: Distinctive terms. Keep this tight: one keyword hit alone lifts a bill to the threshold, so a loose list turns semantic matching into keyword matching.

name.description: A short name for the topic, e.g. 'renter protections'.

negative_examples.description: Bills on this subject but on the other side of it. This is what turns a subject into a position — include them whenever the person expressed a direction, not just an interest.

threshold.description: Score a bill must reach. Use 0.72; the 0.5 default tags everything.

tools.name: save_my_values
tools.title: Save what you care about

tools.description: Score bills against your saved topics using an AI model that runs on this computer. Your topics and the bill text never leave the machine, and there is no per-use cost.

jurisdictions.description: Jurisdictions to score. Omit for everything cloned.

limit.description: Bills to score per jurisdiction. Scoring runs at roughly 25 bills per second, so keep this in the hundreds for an interactive answer.

tools.name: tag_with_local_ai
tools.title: Tag legislation with a local AI model

tools.description: Search the legislation on this computer: bills, roll-call votes, the people named in the data, or a report of what the data covers. Every result carries the repository, commit, and file path it came from.

jurisdictions.description: Locale codes (`il`, `usa`) or Open Civic Data ids such as `ocd-jurisdiction/country:us/state:il/government` or `ocd-division/country:us/state:il/sldl:4`. Omit for everything cloned.

min_confidence.description: How certain a name match must be before anything is attributed to that person. Defaults to medium.

min_score.description: Lowest topic score to include. Defaults to the topic's threshold.

person.description: A legislator's name, matched against sponsors and voters. If it comes back ambiguous, ask which person is meant rather than choosing.

subject.description: A subject term the jurisdiction assigned.

tag.description: A topic from save_my_values. Ranks and filters results by score.

text.description: Words that must all appear in the bill, matched as whole words.

type.description: bills: legislation. votes: roll calls. people: the names present in the data. coverage: what the data can and cannot answer.

tools.name: query
tools.title: Search cloned legislation

resources.description: The topics recorded as yours, and the jurisdictions being tracked. Open this to check whether it describes what you actually meant.
resources.name: values
resources.title: Your saved values

resources.description: What this folder is, how to run it yourself, and how to publish it.
resources.name: readme

resources.description: Which jurisdictions are cloned, how much legislation each has, and whether it publishes individual votes.
resources.name: coverage
resources.title: What your local data covers

arguments.description: Your state, e.g. Illinois — optional, Claude will ask if omitted.
arguments.name: state

arguments.description: What you care about, in your own words — optional.
